extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications people, spokespeople, and agencies who pitch journalists and distribute press releases
extracted.subtask_short: writing media pitches and press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and timing personalized media pitches and accompanying press releases so they are newsworthy and journalist-friendly. Emphasizes relevance, brevity, structure, personalization, timing, follow-up etiquette, and supporting assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release: Formal, full announcement intended for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the formal announcement; typically attached or linked after pitching. Best practice noted: pitch first, then send press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch: Personalized email/message to specific journalist suggesting story angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pitch should be targeted and tailored; recommended to send a pitch first and follow with the press release if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to journalist's beat and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance: 33% of survey responses about 'perfect pitch' emphasized relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches must be relevant to the journalist's beat and the outlet's audience; make clear why this story fits their coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and scannability
rubrics_metrics.description: 91% of journalists prefer pitches under 200 words; brief, scannable; 4-5 paragraphs max.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep copy concise and easy to scan — short sentences, paragraph breaks, and priority information first to be readable in a few minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line tells the story; lead with the news; 5Ws clear immediately; jargon-free; readable in a few minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the subject line informative, put the news up front, ensure who/what/when/where/why are quickly apparent, and avoid jargon or unnecessary background before the main point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference journalist's past work; tailor to their beat; avoid mass emails; address by name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate familiarity with the journalist's previous reporting and explain why the story matters to their specific audience. At minimum personalize the subject line and first sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass/generic outreach and promotional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists hate mass-blast generic emails and promotional language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send blast emails, use overly promotional wording, or pitch content that reads like marketing copy. Tailor to the reporter instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'just checking in' follow-ups, multiple follow-ups; one polite follow-up after 3-5 days then leave alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit follow-ups to a single polite note within 3–5 days; avoid repeated nudges or pushy check-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication channel preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists prefer email; calling instead of email is disliked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use email as the primary outreach channel unless the journalist indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link and asset hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists hate broken links and being asked to 'ask if interested' for multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include working links and provide multimedia and supporting assets upfront rather than making reporters request them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness (not press release for non-news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases for non-news are disliked; pitches should present a clear news angle or exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the content is genuinely newsworthy and articulates a clear angle or exclusive opportunity for the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line that summarizes news in <80 chars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep subject lines short (under 80 characters) and summarizing the story so editors can assess relevance quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized opening (explicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized opening referencing journalist's past work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a sentence that references a recent piece or the reporter's beat to show personalization and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with the news concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: The news in 1-2 sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the core news or hook immediately in one to two sentences before background detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain audience relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Why their audience cares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out why the story matters to the outlet's readers/viewers/listeners — the direct audience impact or hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: State available resources and opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: What's available (interviews, data, exclusives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List what you can provide: spokespeople for interviews, data sets, embargoed access, or exclusives to increase news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release attached or linked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link the full press release rather than expecting the journalist to ask for it; make it easy to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide direct contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct contact info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, direct contact details (phone, email) for immediate follow-up or interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable response window
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable response window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate any timing constraints or windows for response, but keep expectations realistic for journalists' schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: One polite follow-up then disengage
rubrics_metrics.description: One polite follow-up after 3-5 days; then leave alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single courteous reminder is acceptable; further persistence is likely counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: best days and times to send
rubrics_metrics.description: Send Tuesday-Thursday, mid-morning local time; avoid Mondays and Fridays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid Mondays (inbox overflow) and Fridays (weekend mode); target mid-morning local time midweek for best attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer exclusives strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer exclusives to top-tier outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider giving exclusive access or embargoed information to priority outlets to increase pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multimedia up front
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multimedia upfront (don't ask 'if interested').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link images, video, or other assets in the initial outreach to remove friction for storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid broken links and messy assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken links are a major negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test all links and ensure attachments are accessible and clearly labeled to avoid wasting a journalist's time.
